details:
COSMIC TRACE: An Interactive 3D Solar System and Near-Earth Object Explorer

Project Overview

COSMIC TRACE is an interactive 3D astronomy platform designed to make space science more accessible, engaging, and understandable. It transforms astronomical information and NASA data into an immersive digital experience where users can explore the Solar System, investigate planetary motion, and discover information about near-Earth asteroids.

Rather than presenting astronomical information only through static images, charts, or text, COSMIC TRACE allows users to interact directly with a three-dimensional representation of our planetary system.

What We Developed

We developed a browser-based 3D space exploration website featuring several interconnected components:

1. Interactive 3D Solar System

The platform presents the Sun and eight planets in a navigable three-dimensional environment. Users can explore the planetary system, zoom in and out, rotate their viewpoint, select individual planets, and access scientific information.

Planetary motion is represented using approximate orbital elements. Visual distances and planetary sizes are adjusted to make the Solar System easier to explore on screen.

2. Planetary Information Explorer

Users can select planets to access scientific information, including their physical characteristics, orbital periods, eccentricities, distances, and other astronomical measurements.

The platform also provides contextual information to help users understand the scale and motion of planetary objects.

3. Near-Earth Object Explorer

COSMIC TRACE incorporates NASA’s Near-Earth Object Web Service (NeoWs) to retrieve information about asteroids approaching Earth.

Users can explore available asteroid information, including object names, estimated diameters, close-approach dates, relative velocities, and potentially hazardous classifications.

4. Interactive Asteroid Belt

The website includes a three-dimensional illustrative asteroid belt that helps users visualize the distribution of objects between Mars and Jupiter.

Its generated positions are intended for educational visualization rather than representing the verified real-time positions of individual asteroids.

5. NASA Astronomy and Image Data

COSMIC TRACE integrates NASA resources, including:

* NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) data.

* NASA Near-Earth Object Web Service (NeoWs).

* NASA Image and Video Library.

These resources provide users with access to astronomy-related information and imagery beyond the 3D visualization.

6. Scientific Information and Data Sources

The platform includes a dedicated Data Sources and Scientific Accuracy section explaining the datasets, astronomical approximations, visualization limitations, and external scientific resources used by the project.

How Does It Address the Challenge?

COSMIC TRACE addresses the challenge of making astronomical information easier to explore and understand through interactive visualization.

Astronomical datasets can be difficult for beginners to interpret because they often contain numerical measurements, technical terminology, and information distributed across multiple scientific platforms.

Our solution connects these different forms of information through one interactive environment. Users can move between the 3D Solar System, planetary information, and NASA asteroid datasets without needing advanced astronomy knowledge.

By combining scientific information with interactive 3D visualization, COSMIC TRACE creates an accessible way to investigate the relationships between celestial objects and discover more about our Solar System.

Why Is It Important?

Understanding space is not limited to professional astronomers. Planetary motion, asteroids, and near-Earth objects are subjects that can interest students, educators, and the general public.

COSMIC TRACE aims to reduce the barrier between complex astronomical data and everyday users. It encourages curiosity, supports informal science learning, and demonstrates how publicly available scientific information can be transformed into meaningful interactive experiences.

It also highlights the importance of studying near-Earth objects and understanding the scientific information used to monitor them.

Technologies and Resources

* HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript.

* Three.js for three-dimensional rendering.

* NASA Open APIs.

* NASA Near-Earth Object Web Service.

* NASA Image and Video Library.

* NASA/JPL Solar System Dynamics reference resources.

* GitHub Pages for public web hosting.

Project Goal

Our goal is to create an accessible digital gateway to space exploration: a platform where users do not simply read about the Solar System but interact with its objects, investigate astronomical information, and develop a deeper appreciation of the science behind our universe.

COSMIC TRACE — Explore the Solar System. Discover the Data. Understand Our Universe.
